ledger.claim: This trip is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and a detour on those lines costs the rider nothing. The ledger fixes quoted_fare_sgd at SGD 22.00 and total_charged at SGD 25.20, and the entire SGD 3.20 gap is the single ERP line. The only pass-through lines POL-RD-11(a) allows on top of the quote are ERP and tolls actually crossed, a properly chargeable airport surcharge and waiting_time_fee — and this record shows airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00, with the trip ending at Keppel Basin rather than originating at an airport. The excess of SGD 3.20 over the quote is therefore refundable to the rider in full under POL-RD-11(a), and SGD 3.20 is the whole of the contested amount.

The disputed line charges for the gantry 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' at lat 1.34, lng 103.78, charged at 2026-09-21T11:43:00. The trace's closest approach to that gantry is 7482.07 m, at fix index 65, timestamped 2026-09-21T11:40:50, and the derived block records gap_brackets_closest_approach as false and across_gap_distance_m as null. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of it as a crossing; 7482 m is nowhere near that radius. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is, under POL-RD-09(4), a billing-integrity failure refundable in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists — and that limb expressly does not trigger POL-RD-10(8).

The trace is clean and dense enough that its silence about this gantry is meaningful rather than a data gap: 169 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, running from first_fix_at 2026-09-21T11:30:00 to last_fix_at 2026-09-21T11:58:00. None of the impairment limbs in POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires on this trace — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so no down-weighting or corroboration rule is engaged. The charge timestamp 11:43:00 falls inside the traced window, so the trace was in a position to record a crossing and records none.

The driver's own counterparty statement on file concedes the route 'was longer than expected' and states that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt'. That is the party who drove the trip declining to support the charge, and it lines up with the ledger's own derived data, which marks the gantry on_optimal_route false and reports off_optimal_route_total of SGD 3.20 against an on_optimal_route_total of SGD 0.00. The rider's account is corroborated by the driver and by the platform's own arithmetic, not merely asserted.

On POL-RD-01 the deviation is established on this trip's own trace: trace_distance_km 16.0 against optimal_distance_km 12.5 is an excess of 3.5 km, or 28.00%, so both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and the trace figure governs where it and the trip record are compared. The rider does not, however, ask for a distance or time refund on that finding, because POL-RD-11 confines the remedy on an upfront-quoted trip. The finding matters only because it confirms the vehicle travelled a different corridor from the booked optimal route; the operative fact for the money remains the trace's 7.5 km clearance from the charged gantry.

The rider has carried the initial burden under POL-RD-08: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-09114 and the same 2026-09-21 trip window, and the excess of 3.5 km / 28.00% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12, and none is put forward with an artifact behind it. A general assertion that the route was longer than expected discharges nothing.

There is no traffic advisory in the pool that could exonerate any part of this route. I disclose the impairment expressly: EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING, its only issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it can carry no fact. Under POL-GEN-02(3) its absence is itself citable, and on that absence POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all — no advisory names a road, expressway segment or junction, and no validity window can be tested. The driver has in any event invoked no closure or advisory.

The chat log holds exactly one message, and it is the rider's, sent at 2026-09-21T11:53:00: 'The booking was quoted at SGD 22.00; why is there an ERP line?' Its waypoint_hint is null, it names no road or place, and it was sent after the disputed charge at 11:43:00. It cannot be an instruction to take a detour or make an additional stop, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver, and POL-RD-09(3) does not defeat the ERP refund because the charge was not rider-caused.

The rider's claim does not rest on any repeat-deviation or inflated theory, and I put the boundaries on the record rather than stretch them. The excess of 28.00% and 3.5 km sits below both materiality limbs in POL-RD-01 (50% and 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 profile check is not triggered by materiality, and on the profile itself deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06. The rider asks only for the SGD 3.20 the ledger added on top of an already-fixed quote.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare was fixed at booking at SGD 22.00 and the charged total of SGD 25.20 exceeds it only by the ERP line (derived.money.charged_over_quote = 3.20). POL-RD-11 therefore governs, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The 3.5 km / 28% the trace records costs the rider nothing on the fare lines.

Taking the trace at face value, the excess of 3.5 km (28% of the 12.5 km optimal) clears POL-RD-01's two establishment tests (0.8 km and 20%) but is well below both materiality tests (8.0 km absolute and 50%). The deviation is therefore not MATERIAL, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged, and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral can issue on this trip.

Even if the driver profile were consulted under POL-RD-06, the only counters that clause names are clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, so neither the three-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test is met and no repeat-deviation pattern exists.

The driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him by naming a specific artifact (EV-FARE-09114, fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE) and a specific clause (POL-RD-11). With the distance and time lines closed by POL-RD-11, the rider's recovery on this fare is confined to the pass-through lines alone.

The most the rider can recover is the single contested ERP line of SGD 3.20, and only as a standalone pass-through correction: POL-RD-09 settles third-party and government-set charges separately from the fare and never counts them twice, so the 3.20 can never be added on top of any fare recomputation, and no distance or time component of the SGD 25.20 charge is disturbed. The rider's wider framing that the SGD 22.00 booking was mispriced is not supported.

No traffic advisory is on record for this trip - EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 - so no closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 can be run on this bundle. That makes no difference to the money: on an upfront-quoted fare the excess is non-refundable under POL-RD-11 whether it is excused or not.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. Everything turns on one charge line: the SGD 3.20 ERP line for the gantry 'Bukit Merah Central westbound', charged at 2026-09-21T11:43:00 on trip TRP-09114. Rider — you are refunded the full SGD 3.20 you contested, which is the whole of the contested amount. Your ride was an upfront-quoted fare: the booking quoted SGD 22.00 and the ledger's total_charged is SGD 25.20. The entire SGD 3.20 difference is that single ERP line — airport_surcharge and waiting_time_fee are both 0.00, and the base, distance, time and platform-fee lines all sit inside the SGD 22.00 quote. The GPS trace for this trip is complete and unimpaired: 169 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, running 11:30:00 to 11:58:00. Against that trace the gantry's coordinates (lat 1.34, lng 103.78) lie 7,482.07 m from the nearest fix, index 65 at 11:40:50 — nowhere near the 250 m radius POL-RD-09 uses to treat a fix as a crossing. The vehicle never passed the gantry, so under POL-RD-09(4) the line is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not any deviation exists; that limb expressly does not trigger POL-RD-10(8) where it is the only unmatched line. POL-RD-11(a) reaches the same SGD 3.20 independently: on an upfront quote only pass-throughs actually incurred (ERP and tolls crossed, a properly chargeable airport surcharge, waiting_time_fee) may sit on top of the quoted fare, and this one was not incurred. The final amount payable is rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and SGD 3.20 is unchanged. Driver — nothing is found against you on the money and nothing is taken from you. The trace records 16.0 km against the 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km (28.00%), which clears POL-RD-01's two establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) but is below both materiality thresholds (50% and 8.0 km absolute), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral issues; in any event your profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists. POL-RD-11 means the distance and time charges on an upfront-quoted trip are fixed at booking, so no fare recomputation runs against you, and your unrecovered cost on an unjustified detour is not recoverable from the rider under that clause. Your own statement that the route 'was longer than expected' but that you 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt' corroborates the trace; note that a counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier, so it supports the finding but does not enter the confidence cap. Confidence is 0.95, within the cap of 1.0: the deciding fact — that the gantry was never crossed — is carried by two independent artifacts at weight 1.0, the GPS trace EV-GPS-09114 and the fare breakdown EV-FARE-09114. Claims considered: both sides agree POL-RD-11 governs and that the only recoverable item on this fare is the SGD 3.20 ERP line — accepted, and it is the outcome. The rider's POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity claim — accepted, producing both the refund and the referral above. The rider's POL-RD-01 deviation finding of 3.5 km / 28.00% — accepted, but on an upfront quote it moves no money. The POL-RD-06 materiality and repeat-pattern points from both sides — accepted; no material deviation, no pattern, no conduct referral. The rider's POL-RD-07 trace-integrity claim — accepted; the trace is unimpaired, so no corroboration or down-weighting rule is engaged. The rider's POL-RD-04 chat-log claim — accepted; the log holds one rider message at 11:53:00 with waypoint_hint null, naming no road or place and sent after the 11:43:00 charge, so it is no detour instruction and POL-RD-09(3) does not defeat the ERP refund. The rider's POL-RD-03 point that no advisory exists — accepted; the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-09114-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0, so no closure or advisory can exonerate anything. A POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral is recorded in the rulings list; it rides with the money and does not displace it. Open question for the reviewer, which belongs here rather than in the referrals list: why a gantry 7.5 km off the driven corridor was billed at all — the record shows no system cause, and the reviewer may wish to trace the ERP billing source.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: refund as a standalone pass-through correction the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line charged at 2026-09-21T11:43:00 on TRP-09114 — the GPS trace never comes within the 250 m match radius of the gantry (nearest fix 7,482.07 m), so the line is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded whether or not a deviation exists.
